name: John son of Zebedee
title: One of the Twelve
tagline: A fisherman’s son from Galilee; with Peter and James, one of the three Jesus took aside.
story: A fisherman on the sea of Galilee, son of Zebedee and brother of James; with Peter and James, one of three Jesus took aside.

periods.title: With Jesus
periods.sub: The Gospels, in the harmony’s order

periods.title: After Scripture

entries.title: Fishing near Capernaum
entries.text: Scripture does not name their town. They were fishing on the sea of Galilee near Capernaum when called, and went with Jesus to the house of Simon and Andrew there (Mark 1:19–21, 29).

entries.title: In his father’s boat
entries.text: Fishermen in their father’s boat on the sea of Galilee (Matt 4:21; Mark 1:19–20), “partners with Simon” (Luke 5:10).

entries.title: Son of Zebedee
entries.text: Son of Zebedee, who was in the boat with his sons mending nets when Jesus called them, and who had “hired servants” (Matt 4:21; Mark 1:20).

entries.title: His mother’s request
entries.text: Their mother is “the mother of Zebedee’s children”, who asked Jesus for the places at his right and left (Matt 20:20–21) and watched the crucifixion from afar (Matt 27:55–56).

entries.title: Salome? An inference
entries.text: Mark names “Salome” where Matthew has “the mother of Zebedee’s children” among the women at the cross (Mark 15:40; Matt 27:56). Taking her to be Salome is an inference from comparing the two lists; our people data makes it.

entries.title: Cousins of Jesus? A view
entries.text: Some writers go further and make Salome the sister of Jesus’ mother (John 19:25), which would make James and John cousins of Jesus. Camerlynck (1910) reports this and judges that “the relationship of St. James to Jesus remains doubtful”.

entries.title: James’s brother
entries.text: His brother was James, killed by Herod (Matt 4:21; Acts 12:2).

entries.title: In the upper room
entries.text: He is named third among the Eleven in the upper room (Acts 1:13).

entries.title: The lame man at the temple gate
entries.text: With Peter he goes up to the temple at the hour of prayer, where a lame man is healed (Acts 3:1–11).

entries.title: Before the council
entries.text: Before the council the leaders see “the boldness of Peter and John” and that they are “unlearned and ignorant men” (Acts 4:13).

entries.title: Sent to Samaria
entries.text: The apostles send Peter and John to Samaria; they pray for the believers, then preach “in many villages of the Samaritans” on the way back (Acts 8:14–25).

entries.title: “Pillars” at Jerusalem
entries.text: Paul names “James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars” in Jerusalem (Gal 2:9).

entries.title: Patmos
entries.text: The writer of Revelation calls himself John and says he “was in the isle that is called Patmos, for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ” (Rev 1:9). Whether he is this John is disputed.

entries.title: Irenaeus, Against Heresies 3.1.1
entries.text: John “did himself publish a Gospel during his residence at Ephesus in Asia”.

entries.title: Irenaeus, Against Heresies 3.3.4
entries.text: The church at Ephesus had “John remaining among them permanently until the times of Trajan”. Irenaeus also passes on, from hearers of Polycarp, that John rushed out of a bath-house at Ephesus on seeing the heretic Cerinthus inside.

entries.title: Irenaeus, Against Heresies 5.30.3
entries.text: The Revelation “was seen no very long time since, but almost in our day, towards the end of Domitian’s reign”.

entries.title: Eusebius, Church History 3.39.6, on Papias
entries.text: There were “two persons in Asia that bore the same name, and … two tombs in Ephesus, each of which, even to the present day, is called John’s.”

cols.label: Matthew 4 · In the boat with Zebedee

verses.text: And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them.
And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him.
And when he had gone a little further thence, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in the ship mending their nets.
And straightway he called them: and they left their father Zebedee in the ship with the hired servants, and went after him.
And so was also James, and John, the sons of Zebedee, which were partners with Simon. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.
And when they had brought their ships to land, they forsook all, and followed him.
And the two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.
Then Jesus turned, and saw them following, and saith unto them, What seek ye? They said unto him, Rabbi, (which is to say, being interpreted, Master,) where dwellest thou?
He saith unto them, Come and see. They came and saw where he dwelt, and abode with him that day: for it was about the tenth hour.
One of the two which heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.

accounts.title: On the mountain at the transfiguration

verses.text: And after six days Jesus taketh Peter, James, and John his brother, and bringeth them up into an high mountain apart,
And was transfigured before them: and his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light.
And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.
Then answered Peter, and said unto Jesus, Lord, it is good for us to be here: if thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.
While he yet spake, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.
And when the disciples heard it, they fell on their face, and were sore afraid.
And Jesus came and touched them, and said, Arise, and be not afraid.
And when they had lifted up their eyes, they saw no man, save Jesus only.
¶ And after six days Jesus taketh with him Peter, and James, and John, and leadeth them up into an high mountain apart by themselves: and he was transfigured before them.
And his raiment became shining, exceeding white as snow; so as no fuller on earth can white them.
And there appeared unto them Elias with Moses: and they were talking with Jesus.
And Peter answered and said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.
For he wist not what to say; for they were sore afraid.
And there was a cloud that overshadowed them: and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.
And suddenly, when they had looked round about, they saw no man any more, save Jesus only with themselves.
¶ And it came to pass about an eight days after these sayings, he took Peter and John and James, and went up into a mountain to pray.
And as he prayed, the fashion of his countenance was altered, and his raiment was white and glistering.
And, behold, there talked with him two men, which were Moses and Elias:
Who appeared in glory, and spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem.
But Peter and they that were with him were heavy with sleep: and when they were awake, they saw his glory, and the two men that stood with him.

And it came to pass, as they departed from him, Peter said unto Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias: not knowing what he said.
While he thus spake, there came a cloud, and overshadowed them: and they feared as they entered into the cloud.
And there came a voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.
And when the voice was past, Jesus was found alone. And they kept it close, and told no man in those days any of those things which they had seen.
Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;
Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus;
Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
And Simon he surnamed Peter;
And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:
And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,
And Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house.
Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphæus, and Simon called Zelotes,
And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.

And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.

claim.text: John’s Gospel names only Andrew; that the other was John comes from later writers such as Ishodad of Merv (about 850).
His brother, called with him and named with him as Boanerges (Mark 1:19; 3:17).
A fishing partner (Luke 5:10); sent with him to prepare the passover (Luke 22:8); with him at the temple, before the council and in Samaria (Acts 3:1; 4:13; 8:14).
From the cross Jesus gave his mother to “the disciple standing by, whom he loved”, who “took her unto his own home” (John 19:26–27), if that disciple is John.
With James and Cephas he gave Paul and Barnabas “the right hands of fellowship” (Gal 2:9).
His father, left in the boat “with the hired servants” (Mark 1:20).

family.text: Son of Zebedee, who was in the boat with his sons mending nets when Jesus called them, and who had “hired servants” (Matt 4:21; Mark 1:20).
Their mother is “the mother of Zebedee’s children”, who asked Jesus for the places at his right and left (Matt 20:20–21) and watched the crucifixion from afar (Matt 27:55–56).

Mark names “Salome” where Matthew has “the mother of Zebedee’s children” among the women at the cross (Mark 15:40; Matt 27:56). Taking her to be Salome is an inference from comparing the two lists; our people data makes it.

Some writers go further and make Salome the sister of Jesus’ mother (John 19:25), which would make James and John cousins of Jesus. Camerlynck (1910) reports this and judges that “the relationship of St. James to Jesus remains doubtful”.
His brother was James, killed by Herod (Matt 4:21; Acts 12:2).

identifications.text: John’s Gospel never names John son of Zebedee. It speaks of “the disciple whom Jesus loved”, who leaned on Jesus at the supper, and says this disciple “wrote these things” (John 13:23; 21:20, 24).

Irenaeus (about 180) names the writer as “John, the disciple of the Lord, who also had leaned upon His breast”, and Polycrates of Ephesus (about 190) speaks of the John “who reclined upon the bosom of the Lord”. This page follows that identification wherever it shows the beloved disciple.
Ishodad of Merv (about 850) says the unnamed disciple with Andrew in John 1:35–40 “was John, the son of thunder; for he concealed his name, out of modesty”.

Our people data also attaches to this John the “John” of Galatians 2:9 and the John of Revelation (Rev 1:1, 4, 9; 21:2; 22:8). Both are identifications; the second is disputed (see the question below).

scripture.text: Jesus told James and John, “Ye shall indeed drink of the cup that I drink of” (Mark 10:39).
Of the beloved disciple a saying went round “that that disciple should not die: yet Jesus said not unto him, He shall not die” (John 21:23).
Revelation’s John was on Patmos “for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ” (Rev 1:9).
Scripture does not record his death. Acts last shows him in Samaria (Acts 8:14–25) and then names him only as James’s brother (Acts 12:2).

The Revelation “was seen no very long time since, but almost in our day, towards the end of Domitian’s reign”.

argument.text: Irenaeus has him at Ephesus “until the times of Trajan”; Polycrates says he “sleeps at Ephesus”; Jerome says he died “worn out by old age”.

views.label: Killed, like his brother
views.holders: Papias’s second book, as reported by Philip of Side (5th century) and George Hamartolus (9th century)

argument.text: George Hamartolus says Papias wrote that John “was killed by the Jews, and thereby evidently fulfilled, together with his brother, Christ’s prophecy concerning them”. Lightfoot and Harmer (1891) print the first report with a question mark on its attribution to Philip of Side.

items.q: Is the John of Revelation the apostle John?
items.full: Is the John of Revelation the apostle John?

views.label: Yes
views.holders: Justin Martyr (mid-2nd century); Eusebius reports it as said (about 325)

argument.text: Justin speaks of “a certain man with us, whose name was John, one of the apostles of Christ, who prophesied, by a revelation that was made to him”.

views.label: Another John
views.holders: Dionysius of Alexandria (about 250s), quoted by Eusebius; Eusebius himself suggests the “presbyter John” of Papias

argument.text: Dionysius does not deny the book is “the work of one John” but “cannot readily admit that he was the apostle, the son of Zebedee”, judging from its style. Eusebius thinks it “probable” that the second John of Papias “saw the Revelation”.

views.label: The apostle John wrote all three
views.holders: Irenaeus (c. 180); Dionysius of Alexandria for 1 John (c. 250s); B. F. Westcott; A. Plummer; Robert Law; William Smith; M. G. Easton

argument.text: Irenaeus quotes 1 and 2 John as the work of “John, the disciple of the Lord”. Westcott argues that “the elder” marks a unique standing and fits the aged apostle, and Law notes that an apostle could call himself an elder, as Peter does. Plummer holds that the case for 2 John carries 3 John with it.

views.label: The apostle wrote 1 John; John the Elder wrote 2 and 3 John
views.holders: “Many” in Jerome's day (392); raised as an open question by Eusebius (c. 325); A. E. Brooke (1912)

argument.text: Papias, as quoted by Eusebius, names two Johns: the apostle, and “the presbyter John”, a disciple of the Lord. Eusebius adds the report of two tombs at Ephesus, each called John's. Jerome says many held the last two letters to be the presbyter's. Brooke finds this best supported by tradition and by the letters themselves, while leaving the Elder's relation to the apostle an unsolved mystery.

views.label: Different hands, or none of them the apostle's
views.holders: Joseph Scaliger (1540–1609); F. C. Baur, H. J. Holtzmann, Pfleiderer and von Soden, as reported by Robert Law (1915)

argument.text: Scaliger rejected all three letters as not the apostle's. Baur and others argued that the Gospel and 1 John had different authors, Baur explaining the likeness as imitation; Jülicher, Wrede and Wernle, by contrast, accepted a single author.

items.from: Asked on the The letters of John page

views.label: The last decade of the first century

argument.text: The state of the church, and false teaching that matches Cerinthus in Asia at the end of the century.
A long gap after Revelation, the tone of an old man, and a clear stand against Gnosticism.

views.label: The close of the first century

argument.text: Smith gives the date without reasons.
Papias and Polycarp already knew 1 John, so it cannot be later than the first decade of the second century.

views.label: Before AD 70
views.holders: An older reading with no holder named in the sources consulted; recorded and rejected by Plummer

argument.text: It took “it is the last time” to mean the eve of Jerusalem's fall. Plummer answers that Jerusalem had fallen at least a dozen years before the probable date.

views.label: 2 and 3 John soon after 1 John, from the same place
views.holders: A. Plummer; B. F. Westcott; M. G. Easton

argument.text: The short letters share formulas with each other and take 1 John's teaching for granted.

items.q: John’s Gospel never names John son of Zebedee or his brother James; it mentions only “the sons of Zebedee” (John 21:2).
Scripture does not say that John lived at Ephesus, or how or when he died.
John 19:27 says the beloved disciple took Jesus’ mother “unto his own home”; Scripture does not say where that was.
1 John gives no writer’s name, and 2 and 3 John are from “the elder”; who wrote them is discussed on the Letters pages.

verses.40004021: And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them.
verses.40004022: And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him.
verses.40010001: And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.
verses.40010002: Now the names of the twelve apostles are these; The first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;
verses.40010003: Philip, and Bartholomew; Thomas, and Matthew the publican; James the son of Alphaeus, and Lebbaeus, whose surname was Thaddaeus;
verses.40010004: Simon the Canaanite, and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him.
verses.40010005: These twelve Jesus sent forth, and commanded them, saying, Go not into the way of the Gentiles, and into any city of the Samaritans enter ye not:
verses.40017001: And after six days Jesus taketh Peter, James, and John his brother, and bringeth them up into an high mountain apart,
verses.40017002: And was transfigured before them: and his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light.
verses.40017003: And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.
verses.40017004: Then answered Peter, and said unto Jesus, Lord, it is good for us to be here: if thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.
verses.40017005: While he yet spake, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.
verses.40017006: And when the disciples heard it, they fell on their face, and were sore afraid.
verses.40017007: And Jesus came and touched them, and said, Arise, and be not afraid.
verses.40017008: And when they had lifted up their eyes, they saw no man, save Jesus only.
verses.40020020: ¶ Then came to him the mother of Zebedee’s children with her sons, worshipping him, and desiring a certain thing of him.
verses.40020021: And he said unto her, What wilt thou? She saith unto him, Grant that these my two sons may sit, the one on thy right hand, and the other on the left, in thy kingdom.
verses.40020022: But Jesus answered and said, Ye know not what ye ask. Are ye able to drink of the cup that I shall drink of, and to be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with? They say unto him, We are able.
verses.40020023: And he saith unto them, Ye shall drink indeed of my cup, and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared of my Father.
verses.40020024: And when the ten heard it, they were moved with indignation against the two brethren.
verses.40020025: But Jesus called them unto him, and said, Ye know that the princes of the Gentiles exercise dominion over them, and they that are great exercise authority upon them.
verses.40020026: But it shall not be so among you: but whosoever will be great among you, let him be your minister;
verses.40020027: And whosoever will be chief among you, let him be your servant:
verses.40020028: Even as the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
verses.40026037: And he took with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to be sorrowful and very heavy.
verses.40027055: And many women were there beholding afar off, which followed Jesus from Galilee, ministering unto him:
verses.40027056: Among which was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee’s children.
verses.41001019: And when he had gone a little further thence, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in the ship mending their nets.
verses.41001020: And straightway he called them: and they left their father Zebedee in the ship with the hired servants, and went after him.
verses.41001021: And they went into Capernaum; and straightway on the sabbath day he entered into the synagogue, and taught.
verses.41001029: And forthwith, when they were come out of the synagogue, they entered into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
verses.41003013: And he goeth up into a mountain, and calleth unto him whom he would: and they came unto him.
verses.41003014: And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach,
verses.41003015: And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils:
verses.41003017: And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:
verses.41003018: And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,
verses.41003019: And Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house.
verses.41005037: And he suffered no man to follow him, save Peter, and James, and John the brother of James.
verses.41009002: ¶ And after six days Jesus taketh with him Peter, and James, and John, and leadeth them up into an high mountain apart by themselves: and he was transfigured before them.
verses.41009003: And his raiment became shining, exceeding white as snow; so as no fuller on earth can white them.
verses.41009004: And there appeared unto them Elias with Moses: and they were talking with Jesus.
verses.41009005: And Peter answered and said to Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.
verses.41009006: For he wist not what to say; for they were sore afraid.
verses.41009007: And there was a cloud that overshadowed them: and a voice came out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.
verses.41009008: And suddenly, when they had looked round about, they saw no man any more, save Jesus only with themselves.
verses.41009038: ¶ And John answered him, saying, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name, and he followeth not us: and we forbad him, because he followeth not us.
verses.41009039: But Jesus said, Forbid him not: for there is no man which shall do a miracle in my name, that can lightly speak evil of me.
verses.41009040: For he that is not against us is on our part.
verses.41010035: ¶ And James and John, the sons of Zebedee, come unto him, saying, Master, we would that thou shouldest do for us whatsoever we shall desire.
verses.41010036: And he said unto them, What would ye that I should do for you?
verses.41010037: They said unto him, Grant unto us that we may sit, one on thy right hand, and the other on thy left hand, in thy glory.
verses.41010038: But Jesus said unto them, Ye know not what ye ask: can ye drink of the cup that I drink of? and be baptized with the baptism that I am baptized with?
verses.41010039: And they said unto him, We can. And Jesus said unto them, Ye shall indeed drink of the cup that I drink of; and with the baptism that I am baptized withal shall ye be baptized:
verses.41010040: But to sit on my right hand and on my left hand is not mine to give; but it shall be given to them for whom it is prepared.
verses.41010041: And when the ten heard it, they began to be much displeased with James and John.
verses.41010042: But Jesus called them to him, and saith unto them, Ye know that they which are accounted to rule over the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and their great ones exercise authority upon them.
verses.41010043: But so shall it not be among you: but whosoever will be great among you, shall be your minister:
verses.41010044: And whosoever of you will be the chiefest, shall be servant of all.
verses.41010045: For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.
verses.41013003: And as he sat upon the mount of Olives over against the temple, Peter and James and John and Andrew asked him privately,
verses.41013004: Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign when all these things shall be fulfilled?
verses.41014033: And he taketh with him Peter and James and John, and began to be sore amazed, and to be very heavy;
verses.41015040: There were also women looking on afar off: among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome;
verses.42005010: And so was also James, and John, the sons of Zebedee, which were partners with Simon. And Jesus said unto Simon, Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.
verses.42005011: And when they had brought their ships to land, they forsook all, and followed him.
verses.42006012: And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.
verses.42006013: ¶ And when it was day, he called unto him his disciples: and of them he chose twelve, whom also he named apostles;
verses.42006014: Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,
verses.42006015: Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphæus, and Simon called Zelotes,
verses.42006016: And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.
verses.42008051: And when he came into the house, he suffered no man to go in, save Peter, and James, and John, and the father and the mother of the maiden.
verses.42009028: ¶ And it came to pass about an eight days after these sayings, he took Peter and John and James, and went up into a mountain to pray.
verses.42009029: And as he prayed, the fashion of his countenance was altered, and his raiment was white and glistering.
verses.42009030: And, behold, there talked with him two men, which were Moses and Elias:
verses.42009031: Who appeared in glory, and spake of his decease which he should accomplish at Jerusalem.
verses.42009032: But Peter and they that were with him were heavy with sleep: and when they were awake, they saw his glory, and the two men that stood with him.
verses.42009033: And it came to pass, as they departed from him, Peter said unto Jesus, Master, it is good for us to be here: and let us make three tabernacles; one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias: not knowing what he said.
verses.42009034: While he thus spake, there came a cloud, and overshadowed them: and they feared as they entered into the cloud.
verses.42009035: And there came a voice out of the cloud, saying, This is my beloved Son: hear him.
verses.42009036: And when the voice was past, Jesus was found alone. And they kept it close, and told no man in those days any of those things which they had seen.
verses.42009049: ¶ And John answered and said, Master, we saw one casting out devils in thy name; and we forbad him, because he followeth not with us.
verses.42009050: And Jesus said unto him, Forbid him not: for he that is not against us is for us.
verses.42009051: ¶ And it came to pass, when the time was come that he should be received up, he stedfastly set his face to go to Jerusalem,
verses.42009052: And sent messengers before his face: and they went, and entered into a village of the Samaritans, to make ready for him.
verses.42009053: And they did not receive him, because his face was as though he would go to Jerusalem.
verses.42009054: And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said, Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them, even as Elias did?
verses.42009055: But he turned, and rebuked them, and said, Ye know not what manner of spirit ye are of.
verses.42009056: For the Son of man is not come to destroy men’s lives, but to save them. And they went to another village.
verses.42022008: And he sent Peter and John, saying, Go and prepare us the passover, that we may eat.
verses.43001037: And the two disciples heard him speak, and they followed Jesus.
verses.43001038: Then Jesus turned, and saw them following, and saith unto them, What seek ye? They said unto him, Rabbi, (which is to say, being interpreted, Master,) where dwellest thou?
verses.43001039: He saith unto them, Come and see. They came and saw where he dwelt, and abode with him that day: for it was about the tenth hour.
verses.43001040: One of the two which heard John speak, and followed him, was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.
verses.43013023: Now there was leaning on Jesus’ bosom one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved.
verses.43013024: Simon Peter therefore beckoned to him, that he should ask who it should be of whom he spake.
verses.43013025: He then lying on Jesus’ breast saith unto him, Lord, who is it?
verses.43019025: ¶ Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene.
verses.43019026: When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son!
verses.43019027: Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home.
verses.43020002: Then she runneth, and cometh to Simon Peter, and to the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and saith unto them, They have taken away the Lord out of the sepulchre, and we know not where they have laid him.
verses.43020003: Peter therefore went forth, and that other disciple, and came to the sepulchre.
verses.43020004: So they ran both together: and the other disciple did outrun Peter, and came first to the sepulchre.
verses.43020005: And he stooping down, and looking in, saw the linen clothes lying; yet went he not in.
verses.43020006: Then cometh Simon Peter following him, and went into the sepulchre, and seeth the linen clothes lie,
verses.43020007: And the napkin, that was about his head, not lying with the linen clothes, but wrapped together in a place by itself.
verses.43020008: Then went in also that other disciple, which came first to the sepulchre, and he saw, and believed.
verses.43020009: For as yet they knew not the scripture, that he must rise again from the dead.
verses.43020010: Then the disciples went away again unto their own home.
verses.43021001: After these things Jesus shewed himself again to the disciples at the sea of Tiberias; and on this wise shewed he himself.
verses.43021002: There were together Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathanael of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples.
verses.43021003: Simon Peter saith unto them, I go a fishing. They say unto him, We also go with thee. They went forth, and entered into a ship immediately; and that night they caught nothing.
verses.43021004: But when the morning was now come, Jesus stood on the shore: but the disciples knew not that it was Jesus.
verses.43021005: Then Jesus saith unto them, Children, have ye any meat? They answered him, No.
verses.43021006: And he said unto them, Cast the net on the right side of the ship, and ye shall find. They cast therefore, and now they were not able to draw it for the multitude of fishes.
verses.43021007: Therefore that disciple whom Jesus loved saith unto Peter, It is the Lord. Now when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he girt his fisher’s coat unto him, (for he was naked,) and did cast himself into the sea.
verses.43021020: Then Peter, turning about, seeth the disciple whom Jesus loved following; which also leaned on his breast at supper, and said, Lord, which is he that betrayeth thee?
verses.43021021: Peter seeing him saith to Jesus, Lord, and what shall this man do?
verses.43021022: Jesus saith unto him, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee? follow thou me.
verses.43021023: Then went this saying abroad among the brethren, that that disciple should not die: yet Jesus said not unto him, He shall not die; but, If I will that he tarry till I come, what is that to thee?
verses.43021024: This is the disciple which testifieth of these things, and wrote these things: and we know that his testimony is true.
verses.44001013: And when they were come in, they went up into an upper room, where abode both Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip, and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James.
verses.44003001: Now Peter and John went up together into the temple at the hour of prayer, being the ninth hour.
verses.44003002: And a certain man lame from his mother’s womb was carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple which is called Beautiful, to ask alms of them that entered into the temple;
verses.44003003: Who seeing Peter and John about to go into the temple asked an alms.
verses.44003004: And Peter, fastening his eyes upon him with John, said, Look on us.
verses.44003005: And he gave heed unto them, expecting to receive something of them.
verses.44003006: Then Peter said, Silver and gold have I none; but such as I have give I thee: In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth rise up and walk.
verses.44003007: And he took him by the right hand, and lifted him up: and immediately his feet and ankle bones received strength.
verses.44003008: And he leaping up stood, and walked, and entered with them into the temple, walking, and leaping, and praising God.
verses.44003009: And all the people saw him walking and praising God:
verses.44003010: And they knew that it was he which sat for alms at the Beautiful gate of the temple: and they were filled with wonder and amazement at that which had happened unto him.
verses.44003011: And as the lame man which was healed held Peter and John, all the people ran together unto them in the porch that is called Solomon’s, greatly wondering.
verses.44004001: And as they spake unto the people, the priests, and the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees, came upon them,
verses.44004002: Being grieved that they taught the people, and preached through Jesus the resurrection from the dead.
verses.44004003: And they laid hands on them, and put them in hold unto the next day: for it was now eventide.
verses.44004004: Howbeit many of them which heard the word believed; and the number of the men was about five thousand.
verses.44004005: ¶ And it came to pass on the morrow, that their rulers, and elders, and scribes,
verses.44004006: And Annas the high priest, and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as were of the kindred of the high priest, were gathered together at Jerusalem.
verses.44004007: And when they had set them in the midst, they asked, By what power, or by what name, have ye done this?
verses.44004008: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost, said unto them, Ye rulers of the people, and elders of Israel,
verses.44004009: If we this day be examined of the good deed done to the impotent man, by what means he is made whole;
verses.44004010: Be it known unto you all, and to all the people of Israel, that by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, whom ye crucified, whom God raised from the dead, even by him doth this man stand here before you whole.
verses.44004011: This is the stone which was set at nought of you builders, which is become the head of the corner.
verses.44004012: Neither is there salvation in any other: for there is none other name under heaven given among men, whereby we must be saved.
verses.44004013: ¶ Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and perceived that they were unlearned and ignorant men, they marvelled; and they took knowledge of them, that they had been with Jesus.
verses.44004019: But Peter and John answered and said unto them, Whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken unto you more than unto God, judge ye.
verses.44008014: Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John:
verses.44008015: Who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost:
verses.44008016: (For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.)
verses.44008017: Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.
verses.44008018: And when Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money,
verses.44008019: Saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost.
verses.44008020: But Peter said unto him, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.
verses.44008021: Thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter: for thy heart is not right in the sight of God.
verses.44008022: Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee.
verses.44008023: For I perceive that thou art in the gall of bitterness, and in the bond of iniquity.
verses.44008024: Then answered Simon, and said, Pray ye to the Lord for me, that none of these things which ye have spoken come upon me.
verses.44008025: And they, when they had testified and preached the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, and preached the gospel in many villages of the Samaritans.
verses.44012002: And he killed James the brother of John with the sword.
verses.48002009: And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.
verses.66001001: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave unto him, to shew unto his servants things which must shortly come to pass; and he sent and signified it by his angel unto his servant John:
verses.66001009: I John, who also am your brother, and companion in tribulation, and in the kingdom and patience of Jesus Christ, was in the isle that is called Patmos, for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ.
verses.66021002: And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.
verses.66022008: And I John saw these things, and heard them. And when I had heard and seen, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel which shewed me these things.
